# reac-pw / fuzz_headamp

reac-pw's own fuzz target `fuzz_headamp` ([source](source/fuzz_headamp.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over reac-pw 1.0.42 (FreeREAC/reac-pw at f86a30a3).

Builds a PipeWire Props object from the input, keeping a record of what it wrote, and parses its head-amp control keys into a cell array of a fuzz-chosen capacity, with and without a result record; checks the count, the cells, the keys counted, the first refusal and that nothing is written past the capacity.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static library of reac-pw's nine input readers and the harness's box-model table, built from source with libreac's and PipeWire SPA's headers only; neither library is linked.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The reader writes no cell past the capacity it was given; the guard cell after the last one is unchanged ([lines 183-192](source/fuzz_headamp.c#L183-L192)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The return is -1 or a count from 0 to the capacity, and the result reports that count with at least as many head-amp keys seen ([lines 194-205](source/fuzz_headamp.c#L194-L205)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Every cell handed on addresses a channel of the head-amp channel space with a real parameter and a value that parameter takes ([lines 207-219](source/fuzz_headamp.c#L207-L219)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The reader returns -1 exactly for a missing object or one that is not a Props object, and then reports no cells, keys or refusal ([lines 221-237](source/fuzz_headamp.c#L221-L237)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The cells are exactly the well-formed ones the object carries, in the order written, up to the capacity ([lines 239-259](source/fuzz_headamp.c#L239-L259)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Every key under the head-amp prefix that the walk reached is counted, refused ones included ([lines 261-271](source/fuzz_headamp.c#L261-L271)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The refusal reported is the first thing wrong with a key, and none only when every key was accepted ([lines 273-285](source/fuzz_headamp.c#L273-L285)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The parse without a result object returns the same count and writes the same cells as the parse with one ([lines 297-309](source/fuzz_headamp.c#L297-L309)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

| `asan_ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 2 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; ASan+UBSan never fires; memory refused only when forced | [proved](proofs/asan_ubsan_agrees/) |

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch reac-pw` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_headamp.plain` | 54,784 | `61497eebc35c52a0b5decd81ae453deeea1a18220ebf8f6436da6718b13c78b5` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_headamp.ubsan` | 56,128 | `0516fd55d25d0dc25addf9f7563673fa7a309e1f0c2e8c6a4bff0d6c9c8ef9e8` |
| asan | `fuzz_headamp.asan` | 584,952 | `f3e0669d2819724922df0556b11c2dcd22d1e16fe7e0fe1535ce784b34436c47` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_headamp.asan-ubsan` | 586,104 | `53edda9bdeeba1803865babfecb1af6732babe47ab83c64d38cc59a90d717a94` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
